children: U.K. retail sales stalled in October, as consumers remain cautious ahead of the crucial festive shopping season, according to a report released Tuesday. Total retail sales in the U.K. rose 1.5% on year in October, against a 1.6% increase in the same month last year, a report from the British Retail Consortium and KPMG says. "Shoppers and businesses face mounting costs, including rising interest rates and energy bills, adding to the pressures already pushing up prices," BRC Chief Executive Helen Dickinson says. While promotions should help keep shoppers spending during the festive period, January could be a difficult month for many households, the report says. This is due to prospects of higher energy costs, inflation and interest rates, it says. (andrea.figueras@wsj.com)
